macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Fed holds rates steady and signals limited easing
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate at 3.5%-3.75% and projected only one rate cut during the year, citing geopolitical risks and moderating economic momentum. The U.S. dollar strengthened after producer prices rose more than expected.

items.title: U.S. stocks fall sharply after Fed decision
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 768 points, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq dropped more than 1.3% as investors reassessed interest-rate and inflation prospects following the Fed’s decision.

items.title: Global shares retreat after Wall Street records
items.summary: World shares pulled back after the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq reached record closing levels in the prior session. Investors weighed higher oil prices, elevated interest rates and expectations for strong corporate earnings.

items.title: Oil prices rise amid Middle East tensions
items.summary: Brent crude climbed to about $101.26 per barrel and U.S. crude to roughly $89.66 as geopolitical tensions and attacks involving Iran-backed Houthis supported energy prices.

items.title: Constellation Energy rallies on Google nuclear-power deal
items.summary: Constellation Energy shares rose sharply after the company announced a long-term agreement to supply Google with electricity from nuclear generation, including planned upgrades to existing units.

items.title: Lamb Weston beats quarterly expectations
items.summary: Frozen-potato producer Lamb Weston reported quarterly profit and revenue above its own projections and analyst expectations, sending its shares up 7.5%.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin slide triggers more than $400 million in liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below $84,000 in a sharp intraday move, while Ethereum and the broader crypto market also declined. More than $400 million in long positions were liquidated, with separate market estimates putting total 24-hour liquidations near $549 million.[1][2]

items.title: U.S. government-linked wallets move $103 million in crypto
items.summary: Wallets linked to the U.S. government transferred about $71.56 million in Bitcoin to Coinbase Prime and roughly $31.63 million in BNB. The transfers do not confirm sales but heightened concern about potential additional market supply.[7]

items.title: SEC reportedly clears 3x leveraged Bitcoin and Ethereum funds
items.summary: The SEC approved a Cboe rule allowing six Volatility Shares funds, including products offering triple the daily performance of Bitcoin and Ethereum, to list on a U.S. exchange.[4]

items.title: Cardano introduces compliance-focused token standard
items.summary: Cardano introduced CIP-0113, a token standard that allows issuers of regulated assets to impose transfer restrictions and freeze or seize tokens. The standard is intended for assets such as stablecoins, funds and bonds; ADA fell about 4.5% over 24 hours.[10]

items.title: Sui tests Alibaba Cloud stablecoin payment integration
items.summary: Sui connected Alibaba Cloud services to its Agent Payments system to support per-transaction stablecoin payments on the Sui network. The integration is currently operating on testnet and has not reached mainnet.[6]

items.title: Ripple expands prime-brokerage relationship with Brevan Howard
items.summary: Ripple announced an expanded agreement under which Ripple Prime will provide multi-asset prime brokerage, clearing and financing services to Brevan Howard funds across traditional and digital markets.[9]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day launches on PC and Xbox
items.summary: Microsoft’s third-person shooter Gears of War: E-Day released on October 6 for PC and Xbox Series X/S, making it one of the week’s major game launches.

items.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer releases
items.summary: Secret Mode’s Star Wars: Galactic Racer launched October 6 on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S.

items.title: Xbox shifts future Halo development to Activision
items.summary: Xbox is reportedly transferring development of future Halo stories to Activision amid layoffs and a broader restructuring of its gaming division.

items.title: Hideo Kojima’s Physint reportedly expands to Xbox
items.summary: Microsoft is expected to publish Hideo Kojima’s next action-espionage game, Physint, following an expanded partnership with Kojima Productions.

items.title: Sony announces PS5 QSSR upscaling technology
items.summary: Sony announced Quick Spectral Super Resolution, a new AI-upscaling performance tier developed through its graphics collaboration with AMD.

items.title: Take-Two and Microsoft sign long-term Xbox licensing agreement
items.summary: Take-Two and Microsoft entered a new long-term Xbox Publisher License Agreement, effective September 17, according to a regulatory filing.

items.title: Madison Beer joins Fortnite Icon Series
items.summary: Pop star Madison Beer is reportedly the latest celebrity to receive a Fortnite Icon Series collaboration.

items.title: Diablo 4 will continue receiving support after Diablo 5
items.summary: Diablo 4 director Brent Gibson said Blizzard plans to keep supporting the game even after the eventual release of Diablo 5.

items.title: AI-driven game mashups raise industry concerns
items.summary: New AI tools are enabling users to rapidly create playable crossovers and reverse-engineered game projects, prompting concern about the impact on developers and publishers.

items.title: New PS5 exploit reportedly enables kernel access
items.summary: A newly reported exploit called Relapse is said to provide PS5 kernel access directly from the console without requiring a PC.
